edges.effect_quant: Dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest a small average effect that is directionally consistent but not dramatic.
edges.mechanism: This factor likely influences All-cause mortality through a mix of reserve, disability, social engagement, inflammation, and shared chronic-disease burden rather than one single biochemical pathway. That matters because some of these variables behave partly as markers of physiologic aging and partly as modifiable contributors.
edges.summary: In older adults, dose-response meta-analyses backed by prospective cohorts suggest that slow gait speed tracks with higher risk of all-cause mortality. Most disagreement in the literature is about size, subgroup sensitivity, or dose threshold rather than about whether the relationship exists at all.
edges.caveats: Dose, timing, and baseline risk still matter. Observational edges may partly reflect broader lifestyle patterning, while small trials can overstate benefit if follow-up is short.
